patterns: Language module pattern: pub const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (optional) as &str constants
Handler pattern: extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance as optional fn pointers in LanguageInfo
Query pattern: tree-sitter query strings use capture groups (@name) and field selectors (field_name:) to extract AST nodes
Registration pattern: language added to get_language_info() match arm, get_ts_language() match arm, EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages() array
Test pattern: parse_<lang>() helper; ELEMENT_QUERY validation; extract_inheritance validation; DEFUSE_QUERY validation via SemanticExtractor
Inheritance pattern: walk class/interface/enum node's children to find base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) nodes, extract name field from each

related_issues.title: Add language support for X
related_issues.relevance: Demonstrates pattern of adding new language support; referenced in case study of multi-issue refactoring

constraints: All languages must be unconditionally compiled in (no lang-* feature gates); every registered extension is always available at runtime
tree-sitter-php must be added to workspace.dependencies in Cargo.toml and to aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml dependencies
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for languages that support semantic analysis (def-use sites); optional for languages without clear assignment/declaration semantics
extract_inheritance is required for languages with class/interface/trait inheritance; must walk grammar-specific field names (base_clause, class_interface_clause for PHP)
All new .rs files must include SPDX header: // SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 aptu-coder contributors / // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
No .unwrap() or .expect() in production code paths (test-code exemptions via cfg_attr)
test_coverage: Existing language modules have unit tests for ELEMENT_QUERY (class/function/method/interface/enum extraction), CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY (write/read/writeread sites), and extract_inheritance. Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ validate end-to-end analysis. mod.rs has table-driven tests covering all registered languages.

library_findings.version: not yet in Cargo.lock; latest crates.io version recommended
library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; Grammar defines class_declaration, interface_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration, function_definition nodes; base_clause and class_interface_clause children (not fields) carry inheritance
library_findings.notes: PHP grammar uses base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) as child nodes, not LanguageInfo fields. Method declarations inside class/enum bodies; functions are function_definition at module level. Enums support backing types (int/string) and method declarations.

library_findings.relevant_api: Query::new(), QueryCursor, Node::child_by_field_name(), Node::named_child(), Node::kind(), Node::start_byte(), Node::end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Query strings use @capture_name and field: syntax. Node traversal via parent(), child(), named_child(). Bounds-check all byte slicing: end_byte() <= source.len().

approaches.name: Approach 1: Minimal PHP support (no DEFUSE_QUERY, no extract_inheritance)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY only; register in mod.rs, lang.rs, Cargo.toml; add .php extension to EXTENSION_MAP; add 'php' to supported_languages(). Skip DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance handlers.
pros: Sufficient for basic symbol extraction (functions, methods, classes, interfaces, enums)
cons: Incomplete feature parity with Java, Python, Rust, Kotlin
Likely to receive maintainer feedback requesting DEFUSE_QUERY

approaches.name: Approach 2: Full PHP support with DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance (RECOMMENDED)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, extract_inheritance, and find_receiver_type handlers; register in mod.rs, lang.rs, Cargo.toml; add .php extension and 'php' to supported_languages(); add comprehensive unit tests covering all query types and inheritance extraction.
pros: Full feature parity with Java, Python, Rust, Kotlin
Enables def-use analysis for PHP code (variable tracking, assignment detection)
Enables inheritance analysis (class extends, interface implements)
Receiver type detection for method analysis
Comprehensive test coverage reduces maintenance burden
Aligns with maintainer expectations (DEFUSE_QUERY is standard for object-oriented languages)
cons: Requires careful grammar study to map PHP node kinds to query patterns
DEFUSE_QUERY complexity (local declarations, assignments, identifier reads)
extract_inheritance must walk base_clause and class_interface_clause children correctly

approaches.name: Approach 3: Phased rollout (DEFUSE_QUERY first, extract_inheritance deferred)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and DEFUSE_QUERY; register in mod.rs, lang.rs, Cargo.toml; add .php extension and 'php' to supported_languages(). Defer extract_inheritance to a follow-up PR; set extract_inheritance handler to None initially.
pros: Reduces initial PR scope and review burden
Allows community feedback on DEFUSE_QUERY patterns before inheritance
cons: Maintenance burden split across two reviews
extract_inheritance is critical for class-based code analysis

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP support with DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance). Rationale: PHP is an object-oriented language with class inheritance, interfaces, and traits. The Java, Python, Kotlin, and Rust integrations all include DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance; omitting them from PHP would create inconsistent feature coverage. The tree-sitter-php grammar clearly defines base_clause and class_interface_clause children, making inheritance extraction straightforward. DEFUSE_QUERY patterns (local variable declarations, assignments, identifier reads) are well-established in the codebase and directly applicable to PHP. The additional effort (~100-150 LOC) is justified by full feature parity and maintainer alignment.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @function_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
"
inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node in tree-sitter-php grammar: (1) the node has three fields: attributes (optional attribute_list), body (required declaration_list), and name (required name); (2) base_clause and class_interface_clause are optional child nodes (not fields), appearing as direct children of class_declaration; (3) base_clause is a child node containing one or more name nodes representing the extends parent class; (4) class_interface_clause is a child node containing one or more name nodes representing the implements interfaces; (5) walk node.child_count() and node.child(i), filter for node.kind() == 'base_clause' or 'class_interface_clause', then iterate their named_child() to extract each name node's text. Source: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/php/src/node-types.json and https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js
